recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate supplemental irrigation and improve soil organic carbon to alleviate critical water stress and restore canopy vigor.
recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows severe vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) caused by drought and temperatures above the optimal range (31 °C). Soil chemistry is favorable (pH 6.21, high nitrogen, suitable clay‑loam texture), but low organic carbon limits moisture retention. Prompt irrigation combined with organic matter addition addresses the most urgent agronomic constraints and leverages the strong market price for cotton.
actions: Activate flood irrigation immediately; apply 30‑40 mm of water per hectare each day for the next 5‑7 days, then resume the recommended 7‑10 day schedule.
Incorporate 5‑8 t/ha of well‑decomposed compost or farmyard manure into the root zone to raise organic carbon levels.
Apply a balanced N‑P‑K fertilizer (e.g., 120 kg N, 60 kg P₂O₅, 60 kg K₂O per ha) to support rapid vegetative recovery.
Conduct weekly scouting for aphids, bollworms, and wilt symptoms; deploy bio‑insecticides or Bt‑cotton measures if pest thresholds are exceeded.
Install soil moisture sensors at 20 cm depth and record readings twice daily to fine‑tune irrigation timing.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Vegetation health indices (NDVI) expected to rise above 0.4 within two weeks, reducing water‑stress risk and preserving yield potential; soil organic carbon will improve, enhancing moisture retention for the flowering stage; market‑ready cotton can be harvested with stable profitability.
monitoring_plan: Daily visual check of canopy color, leaf wilting, and soil surface moisture.
Record soil moisture sensor data twice daily; adjust irrigation if moisture falls below 20 % volumetric water content.
Weekly remote‑sensing (drone or satellite) to update NDVI and NDWI values.
Weekly pest scouting reports; trigger IPM actions when pest counts exceed economic thresholds.
Bi‑weekly soil test (organic carbon, nitrogen) to track amendment effectiveness.

steps.finding: Implement immediate supplemental irrigation and improve soil organic carbon to alleviate critical water stress and restore canopy vigor.
actions: Activate flood irrigation immediately; apply 30‑40 mm of water per hectare each day for the next 5‑7 days, then resume the recommended 7‑10 day schedule.
Incorporate 5‑8 t/ha of well‑decomposed compost or farmyard manure into the root zone to raise organic carbon levels.
Apply a balanced N‑P‑K fertilizer (e.g., 120 kg N, 60 kg P₂O₅, 60 kg K₂O per ha) to support rapid vegetative recovery.
Conduct weekly scouting for aphids, bollworms, and wilt symptoms; deploy bio‑insecticides or Bt‑cotton measures if pest thresholds are exceeded.
Install soil moisture sensors at 20 cm depth and record readings twice daily to fine‑tune irrigation timing.
steps.justification: Satellite imagery shows severe vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) caused by drought and temperatures above the optimal range (31 °C). Soil chemistry is favorable (pH 6.21, high nitrogen, suitable clay‑loam texture), but low organic carbon limits moisture retention. Prompt irrigation combined with organic matter addition addresses the most urgent agronomic constraints and leverages the strong market price for cotton.
